facts.raw_span: bilateral photophobia and decreased vision
CD4 count was 24 cells/mm3
HIV RNA level was 175,000 copies/mL
pruritic back rash of crusting erythematous plaques
uncorrected visual acuity was hand motions in both eyes
intraocular pressures were 14 and 9 mm Hg in the right and left eye, respectively
corneal stromal haze, 3+ anterior chamber cell
vitreous cell and haze obscuring retinal vascular details
Cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay: positive
Rapid plasma reagin testing: 1:64 titer
interface dermatitis with spirochetes evident upon hematoxylin-eosin staining
Aqueous fluid from both eyes negative for herpetic viral DNA by PCR

concepts.why: Positive cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay and rapid plasma reagin testing, along with interface dermatitis and spirochetes on skin lesion histopathology, support syphilitic uveitis.
Low CD4 count and high HIV RNA level, along with corneal stromal haze and vitreous cell, support HIV-related uveitis.
Bilateral photophobia and decreased vision, along with vitreous cell and haze, support toxoplasmic retinochoroiditis.
Low CD4 count and high HIV RNA level, along with vitreous cell and haze, support cytomegalovirus retinitis.

Positive cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay and rapid plasma reagin testing, along with interface dermatitis and spirochetes on skin lesion histopathology, support syphilitic retinitis.
Low CD4 count and high HIV RNA level, along with vitreous cell and haze, support HIV-related retinal microvasculopathy.

concepts.preferred_label: Acute Posterior Multifocal Placoid Pigment Epitheliopathy
concepts.why: Bilateral photophobia and decreased vision, along with corneal stromal haze, support acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy.

Positive cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay and rapid plasma reagin testing, along with interface dermatitis and spirochetes on skin lesion histopathology, support syphilitic chorioretinitis.

The patient's presentation of bilateral photophobia and decreased vision, along with the laboratory results and imaging studies, is consistent with syphilitic infection, which is further supported by the positive cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay and the presence of spirochetes in the skin lesion histopathology.

rationales.F01: Bilateral photophobia and decreased vision are non-specific symptoms.
rationales.F02: Low CD4 count increases the risk of opportunistic infections, including HIV-related uveitis and retinitis.
rationales.F03: High HIV RNA level indicates uncontrolled HIV infection, increasing the risk of opportunistic infections.
rationales.F04: Pruritic back rash is consistent with syphilitic rash, which is a manifestation of secondary syphilis.
rationales.F07: Corneal stromal haze and anterior chamber cell are indicative of uveitis, which can be caused by syphilis.
rationales.F08: Vitreous cell and haze are indicative of vitritis, which can be caused by syphilis.
rationales.F09: Positive cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay is diagnostic of neurosyphilis.
rationales.F10: Positive rapid plasma reagin testing is diagnostic of syphilis.
rationales.F11: Interface dermatitis with spirochetes is diagnostic of syphilis.
rationales.F12: Negative aqueous fluid PCR for herpetic viral DNA rules out herpetic uveitis.
